Question: What is the purpose of issuing grades in middle school? This is a serious question and I would love some input from educators. I am a student, it stems from a conversation, and I am trying to gain perspective.
Old_Answer: Huh? For the USA: One needs a measure of where the student “stands” relative to the expected learning for each course/subject in every year of school. Middle school is the transition from elementary school where the grades may be: Exceptional, Satisfactory, Needs more work, Failing; to high school where the grades may be A, B, C, D, F and some with “pluses or minuses”. In my high school our grades were numerical, 75 was failing and the grades went up to 100. The assumption being, if you didn’t absorb and understand at least 75% of the material that you were expected to cover in that subject during that term or year, then you will be lost as you try to advance in the subject’s material in the subsequent years. Simple and logical. How else would the student know if they are truly understanding the required material, if they do not get a Grade from the teachers? By getting a grade in middle school, you are preparing yourself for high school where your GPA may determine your ability to apply to colleges, the US military and/or various jobs. Good luck.
